cause_statement: Windows recorded Explorer.EXE initiating a user-session power-off in the same UTC second as the final durable heartbeat; the normal Windows shutdown sequence followed. This host shutdown terminated the foreground calibration process.

system_events.finding: C:\WINDOWS\Explorer.EXE initiated a power-off of WIGGLER on behalf of WIGGLER\ckytr; reason Other (Unplanned), shutdown type power off.
Kernel power manager initiated a shutdown transition (Power Action Shutdown Off).

negative_or_unavailable_evidence.application_process_crash_or_wer: No matching Application Error or Windows Error Reporting event in the inspected window.
negative_or_unavailable_evidence.resource_exhaustion: No matching Resource-Exhaustion or System event 2004 in the inspected window.
negative_or_unavailable_evidence.defender_security: No Defender detection/remediation event in the inspected window; the only Defender event was normal configuration cleanup during shutdown.
negative_or_unavailable_evidence.sleep_or_unexpected_power_loss: No wake history was reported; the orderly shutdown events, rather than Kernel-Power 41 or EventLog 6008, identify a requested power-off.
negative_or_unavailable_evidence.historical_process_audit: No Security 4688/4689 event was available in the inspected window, so the original Python parent-process chain cannot be reconstructed.

launch_and_lifetime_assessment.launcher_behavior: launcher.py invokes execute_protocol directly in its own Python interpreter; it does not create a detached calibration worker, service, scheduled task, or independent supervisor.
launch_and_lifetime_assessment.conclusion: The calibration was a foreground interpreter workload and was necessarily terminated by the host power-off. The available evidence cannot establish whether its original direct parent was PowerShell, a Codex wrapper, or another interactive-session launcher; regardless, no ordinary child-wrapper arrangement would survive a host shutdown.

infrastructure_recommendation: No runtime or Cardcade change is proposed from this evidence. Detaching the process from an interactive wrapper would not prevent a host power-off. If a future run is authorized, the smallest evidence-supported operational addition is immutable launch metadata (PID, parent PID, session ID, command line, and start time) written before execution, so a future termination can be attributed without relying on unavailable process-audit history.
